title: Mark handoff into a connector chat tour
summary: Two-brand lockup opens, then one continuous dark UI tour: add a connector, three prompts with streamed answers, an authorize click that morphs into a permissions list, and the mark returns as the end card.
use_when: Announcing an integration that plugs one product into an AI assistant
Showing a setup flow end to end: install, ask, act, grant permissions
A calm dark product walkthrough with no cuts and no VO
Partnership launches where both marks share the opening lockup

look.type_style: UI in a neutral grotesk, sentence case, small (prompt text ~4 % H at element zoom, ~1.5 % H at full frame); assistant answers in a book serif; wordmark bold grotesk ~2.5 % H

sfx.event: mark punch-in at open and before the end card
wordmark unfold, lockup and end card settle
button presses, connector add check, authorize
tool-call rows, answer lines, table rows, permission rows landing
camera push toward the authorize dialog

params.partner_mark: second brand glyph + name for the opening lockup and the authorize dialog
params.menu_chips: 3 menu labels, the third is the target
params.connector: name, one-line description (<= 9 words), logo tile
params.answers: 3 assistant replies: bullets with 3 figures; a 3-column table; a 4-row key/value spec
params.permissions: 6 tool rows, each allow / ask / block

notes: One continuous shot (cuts.json: 0 hard, 0 soft), so every row hands over continuous; states change through fades, morphs and camera moves. Music-only reference (126.0 BPM, -12.87 LUFS, no VO); all sfx are planned by the glue rule, not measured. Timings at 0.25 s sheet resolution; spring names chosen without visible overshoot (not measurable at 4 fps). Camera magnitudes are estimates from object widths in cells plus motion.json. Proposed terms (not in vocabulary): accent-tail-typing, focus-isolate-blur, button-to-toggle morph uses morph. Accent sampled by palettegen as #A67668 (anti-aliased); the on-screen accent reads as a warmer orange. Status colours green / amber / red appear only in the permissions row and are not in the palette.
